intended_object: The homeomorphism between the disjoint union of open n-balls, one per n-cell, and the union of the open n-cells of a relative CW complex (taken as a subspace of X). The map on each summand is that cell's characteristic map. Inferred from the docstring and name.
explanation: The map sends (i, y) to `map n i y`. It is bijective because distinct open cells are disjoint, each characteristic map is injective on the open ball, and the union is covered by definition. It is continuous on each summand because the characteristic maps are continuous on the closed ball. It is open because on each summand it is the cell's homeomorphism onto its open cell followed by an inclusion, and that open cell is open in the union. So it is exactly the classical homeomorphism. The ball in `Fin n → ℝ` with the sup norm is Mathlib's own convention for cells in `RelCWComplex`; the resulting cube is homeomorphic to the Euclidean ball. The setting (an arbitrary relative CW complex in a Hausdorff space) is the natural one. I found no Mathlib declaration of this homeomorphism.
